name: C-REACTIVE PROTEIN
description: C-Reactive Protein measures inflammation and infection levels. This acute phase reactant helps diagnose and monitor inflammatory conditions, infections, and cardiovascular risk.

testdetails.instrumentation: Beckman Coulter, Roche Cobas, Abbott Architect

literatureReview: C-Reactive Protein (CRP) is an acute phase reactant produced by liver in response to inflammation, infection, or tissue damage. High sensitivity CRP (hs-CRP) measures low levels for cardiovascular risk assessment. Normal <1 mg/L, intermediate risk 1-3 mg/L, high risk >3 mg/L. Elevated levels indicate infection, autoimmune disease, malignancy, or cardiovascular inflammation. Immunoturbidimetric assay provides high sensitivity and precision. Used for cardiovascular risk stratification, monitoring inflammatory diseases, and detecting occult infections. CRP rises within hours of inflammation onset and returns to normal with resolution. More specific than ESR for acute inflammation. Critical marker for assessing treatment response in inflammatory conditions.
